title: SharePoint: AI citations analytics show how often Copilot cites documents, news and pages
summary: Hold: the description of Restricted Content Discovery overstates what it blocks. Microsoft says it does not affect Copilot experiences using content already open or in use, so administrators must not treat it as excluding every response involving a site's content.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because licensing specific to citation analytics is not yet published.
claims.quote: To access SharePoint, users in your organization need to be assigned a license that includes SharePoint.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included for the published product-level entitlement, and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/sharepoint-online-service-description/sharepoint-online-service-description. Replace the opening licensing statement with: 'Access to SharePoint requires a license that includes SharePoint. Licensing specific to AI citations analytics, including whether it consumes Copilot Credits, is not yet published.' Keep the distinction from advanced-work performance analytics and do not claim that citation analytics has no additional charge.

claims.claim: Prerequisites specific to citation analytics are not yet published.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is under SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.
claims.fix: Keep the path supported by its cited control reference. Add a short note: 'Microsoft's readiness guidance instead labels the final setting Restrict content discovery > On.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/get-ready-copilot-sharepoint-advanced-management#step-3-prevent-accidental-oversharing for that differing label.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: Use PowerShell: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery keeps a site's content out of Microsoft Copilot responses.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't affect experiences that operate on content that's already in use by the user, such as summarizing an open document.
claims.fix: Replace 'Restricted Content Discovery keeps a site's content out of Microsoft Copilot responses' with 'Restricted Content Discovery limits discovery of a site's content in organization-wide search and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, but does not affect experiences using content already in use, such as summarizing an open document'. Keep the following statement about hiding AI entry points and selective use. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/restricted-content-discovery.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery hides the Copilot button and AI entry points on the site.
claims.quote: Users don't see entry points such as the Copilot button, AI actions menus (including creating agents), or Create pages with AI.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a temporary governance control for permissions and governance reviews.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is designed as a temporary governance control that gives organizations time to review and right-size access while continuing their Copilot deployment.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises using Restricted Content Discovery selectively.
claims.quote: Use Restricted Content Discovery selectively. Excessive use can reduce the amount of content available to organization-wide search and Microsoft Copilot experiences

claims.claim: Configuring Restricted Content Discovery requires an organization licensed for Copilot with SharePoint Advanced Management available.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -DelegateRestrictedContentDiscoverabilityManagement $true enables delegation of Restricted Content Discovery management.
claims.quote: If you want site administrators to manage the setting for their own sites, enable delegation by using the following PowerShell command: Set-SPOTenant -DelegateRestrictedContentDiscoverabilityManagement $true

claims.claim: Delegation lets site administrators manage Restricted Content Discovery for their own sites.
claims.quote: When delegation is enabled, site administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery for their sites.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is not documented as a control over citation analytics itself.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint citation analytics Restricted Content Discovery analytics reporting setting. Read Restrict discovery of SharePoint sites and content and Copilot in SharePoint availability; they describe discovery and AI entry points, not an analytics reporting switch.
